title: Immunoinformatics based design and evaluation of a multi-epitope vaccine candidate targeting the envelopment polyprotein of Andes orthohantavirus
abstract: Andes Orthohantavirus is known to be the etiological agent for hantavirus cardiopulmonary syndrome (HCPS), which is a highly dangerous disease with a very high death rate. There is no vaccine available to date to protect against this disease. This project aimed to develop a multi-epitope vaccine for Andes Orthohantavirus using immunoinformatics. Epitopes of CTL, HTL, and B cell types were predicted for the shortlisted Glycoprotein precursor after testing antigenicity, allergenicity, toxicity, and subcellular location. The chosen epitopes were combined using appropriate linkers and β-defensin as an adjuvant to create a multi-epitope vaccine. The final vaccine construct had a length of 296 amino acids and showed excellent antigenicity (0.7297), non-allergenicity, structural stability, and solubility properties. The structure of the vaccine construct showed that 94.6% of residues lie in the preferred areas of the Ramachandran plot, thus ensuring good stereochemistry. Molecular docking and normal mode analysis results confirmed the stable binding of the vaccine construct to TLR-3 receptors. At the same time, immune simulation revealed a fast degradation of antigens, production of antibodies, memory B-cells, and cytokines. In silico cloning integrated the codon-optimized gene with a CAI value of 0.97 and a GC percentage of 49.77% into the plasmid vector pET-28a(+). The designed multi-epitope vaccine displayed good predicted immunogenicity, structure, and expression properties that made it suitable to be used as a potential vaccine candidate against Andes Orthohantavirus infection. Further experimental validation is needed to assess its safety and effectiveness.

elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 所提供的证据并未报告 疫苗 安全性和有效性的实验验证。证据强度中等,因为结果基于计算机预测和模拟。

title: Hantavirus Infections: Virology, Pathogenesis, Clinical Spectrum, and Emerging Therapeutic Frontiers
abstract: Abstract Hantaviruses are rodent-borne zoonotic viruses that cause hemorrhagic fever with renal syndrome (HFRS) in Eurasia and hantavirus pulmonary syndrome (HPS) in the Americas. Despite advances in hantavirus biology and clinical management, no universally approved antiviral therapy exists, and severe HPS remains associated with high mortality. This review summarizes the current understanding of hantavirus virology, epidemiology, pathogenesis, diagnosis, treatment, and prevention, with emphasis on emerging therapeutic strategies. Hantavirus disease is characterized by profound vascular permeability despite limited direct cytopathic injury. Increasing evidence implicates immune-mediated endothelial dysfunction involving β3 integrins, CD8+ T-cell responses, angiopoietin/Tie2 dysregulation, vascular endothelial growth factor signaling, and neutrophil extracellular traps, thereby providing potential targets for antiviral and host-directed therapies. Clinical management remains predominantly supportive. Intravenous ribavirin may benefit patients when administered early in HFRS but has not demonstrated efficacy in established HPS. Venoarterial extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (VA-ECMO) has emerged as an important rescue therapy for severe HPS with cardiopulmonary collapse. Experimental approaches include favipiravir, direct-acting antivirals, convalescent plasma, broadly neutralizing monoclonal antibodies, viral entry and fusion inhibitors, and strategies targeting pathological host responses. Next-generation vaccine platforms, including DNA vaccines, virus-like particle, and structure-guided subunit vaccines, are under investigation. Integrating structural virology, antiviral discovery, immunology, genomic surveillance, and One Health approaches will be essential for developing effective therapeutic strategies.

abstract_zh: 摘要汉坦病毒是啮齿动物传播的人畜共患病毒,在欧亚大陆引起 肾综合征出血热 (HFRS),在美洲引起 汉坦病毒肺综合征 (HPS)。尽管汉坦病毒生物学和临床管理取得了进展,但尚不存在普遍批准的 抗病毒药物 疗法,并且严重的 HPS 仍然与高 死亡率 相关。本综述总结了目前对汉坦病毒病毒学、流行病学、发病机制、诊断、治疗 和预防的理解,重点是新兴的治疗策略。汉坦病毒疾病的特点是尽管直接细胞病变有限,但血管通透性很高。越来越多的证据表明免疫介导的内皮功能障碍涉及 β3 整联蛋白、CD8+ T 细胞反应、血管生成素/Tie2 失调、血管内皮生长因子信号传导和中性粒细胞胞外陷阱,从而为 抗病毒药物 和 宿主 定向治疗提供潜在靶点。临床管理仍然主要是支持性的。在 HFRS 早期给药时,静脉注射利巴韦林可能会使患者受益,但尚未证明对已确定的 HPS 有效。静脉动脉体外膜肺氧合 (VA-ECMO) 已成为治疗伴有心肺衰竭的严重 HPS 的重要救援疗法。实验方法包括法匹拉韦、直接作用的 抗病毒药物、恢复期血浆、广泛中和单克隆抗体、病毒进入和融合抑制剂以及针对病理性 宿主 反应的策略。下一代疫苗平台,包括DNA 疫苗、病毒样颗粒和结构引导亚基疫苗,正在研究中。整合结构病毒学、抗病毒药物 发现、免疫学、基因组监测 和 One Health 方法对于制定有效的治疗策略至关重要。

analysis_zh.scope_and_question: 汉坦病毒 是啮齿类动物传播的人畜共患病毒,在欧亚大陆引起 肾综合征出血热 (HFRS),在美洲引起 汉坦病毒肺综合征 (HPS)。该综述重点关注当前对汉坦病毒病毒学、流行病学、发病机制、诊断、治疗 和预防的理解,重点是新兴的治疗策略。
analysis_zh.evidence_base_and_review_method: 该综述是对汉坦病毒知识现状的全面总结,包括其病毒学、流行病学、发病机制、诊断、治疗 和预防。它不报告具体的数据库、检索日期、资格标准或研究计数。方法部分概述了正在研究的实验方法和治疗策略。
analysis_zh.consensus_and_key_conclusions: 汉坦病毒 疾病的特点是尽管直接细胞病变有限,但血管通透性很高。越来越多的证据表明,涉及 β3 整联蛋白、CD8+ T 细胞反应、血管生成素/Tie2 失调、血管内皮生长因子信号传导和中性粒细胞胞外陷阱等免疫介导的内皮功能障碍是 抗病毒药物 和 宿主 定向治疗的潜在靶点。临床管理仍然主要是支持性的,静脉注射利巴韦林在 HFRS 早期给药时可能使患者受益,但尚未证明对已建立的 HPS 有效。
analysis_zh.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: 对于汉坦病毒感染,尚无普遍批准的 抗病毒药物 疗法,并且严重的 HPS 仍然与高 死亡率 相关。该综述强调需要进一步研究 抗病毒药物 和 宿主 定向疗法,特别是考虑到利巴韦林在 HPS 中的疗效有限。该评论还指出,实验方法正在研究中,但没有提供有关其结果或局限性的具体细节。
analysis_zh.research_and_practice_implications: 整合结构病毒学、抗病毒药物 发现、免疫学、基因组监测 和 One Health 方法对于制定有效的治疗策略至关重要。下一代 疫苗 平台,包括 DNA 疫苗、病毒样颗粒和结构引导亚基 疫苗,正在研究中,可能会提供有希望的预防途径。

title: Rat Hepatitis E Virus and Seoul Hantavirus in Pet Rats, Germany.
abstract: Pet rats represent a reservoir of multiple zoonotic pathogens. We demonstrated that pet rats, previously confirmed to be Seoul orthohantavirus-infected and involved in human infections in Germany, were concurrently infected with rat hepatitis E virus. The high degree of rat hepatitis E virus sequence identity suggests a single incursion event.

title: Hantavirus Transmission Dynamics in the United States: Reservoir Ecology, Environmental and Social Drivers, and Public Health Implications
abstract: Hantavirus pulmonary syndrome (HPS) is a rare but severe rodent-borne zoonosis. As of the end of 2023, the United States had recorded 890 laboratory-confirmed hantavirus cases since surveillance began in 1993, with 35% case fatality and 94% of cases west of the Mississippi River. This narrative review, searched through November 2026, synthesises epidemiological surveillance, reservoir ecology, ecological niche modelling, social-vulnerability analyses, and climate research to explain where and why Sin Nombre virus (SNV) spills over to people. We integrate evidence that SNV is detected in, and infectious virus isolated from, several rodent species beyond the western deer mouse (Peromyscus sonoriensis, formerly P. maniculatus), though independent maintenance is unproven; niche models linking suitability to arid climates and low-intensity development; the 2025 clusters in New Mexico and California; Seoul virus infections linked to pet rats; and the 2026 Andes virus outbreak on a cruise ship, which renewed attention to person-to-person-transmissible hantaviruses. We separate well-established findings from tentative, correlational inferences about biodiversity, social vulnerability, and climate change, and summarise clinical recognition and management. Priorities include taxonomy-aware rodent surveillance, integrated One Health forecasting, diagnosis and referral to centres offering extracorporeal membrane oxygenation, and targeted prevention for rural, Indigenous, and occupationally exposed communities.

As of the end of 2023, the United States had recorded 890 laboratory-confirmed hantavirus cases since surveillance began in 1993, with 35% case fatality and 94% of cases west of the Mississippi River. This narrative review, searched through November 2026, synthesises epidemiological surveillance, reservoir ecology, ecological niche modelling, social-vulnerability analyses, and climate research to explain where and why Sin Nombre virus (SNV) spills over to people. We integrate evidence that SNV is detected in, and infectious virus isolated from, several rodent species beyond the western deer mouse (Peromyscus sonoriensis, formerly P. maniculatus), though independent maintenance is unproven; niche models linking suitability to arid climates and low-intensity development; the 2025 clusters in New Mexico and California; Seoul virus infections linked to pet rats; and the 2026 Andes virus outbreak on a cruise ship, which renewed attention to person-to-person-transmissible hantaviruses. We separate well-established findings from tentative, correlational inferences about biodiversity, social vulnerability, and climate change, and summarise clinical recognition and management. Priorities include taxonomy-aware rodent surveillance, integrated One Health forecasting, diagnosis and referral to centres offering extracorporeal membrane oxygenation, and targeted prevention for rural, Indigenous, and occupationally exposed communities.

abstract_zh: 汉坦病毒肺综合征 (HPS) 是一种罕见但严重的啮齿动物传播的 人兽共患病。自1993年监测开始以来,截至2023年底,美国已记录了890例实验室确诊的汉坦病毒病例,病死率达35%,其中94%的病例发生在密西西比河以西。这篇叙述性综述检索至 2026 年 11 月,综合了流行病学 监测、储存宿主 生态学、生态位模型、社会脆弱性分析和气候研究,以解释 Sin Nombre 病毒 (SNV) 蔓延到人类的地点和原因。我们整合了证据,证明 SNV 在西部鹿鼠(Peromyscus sonoriensis,以前称为 P. maniculatus)以外的几种啮齿动物中检测到并分离出传染性病毒,尽管独立维持尚未得到证实;将适宜性与干旱气候和低强度发展联系起来的利基模型;2025 年新墨西哥州和加利福尼亚州的集群;首尔病毒感染与宠物鼠有关;以及游轮上的 2026 年安第斯山脉病毒 暴发,这再次引起了人们对人际传播汉坦病毒的关注。我们将公认的发现与有关生物多样性、社会脆弱性和气候变化的初步相关推论分开,并总结临床识别和管理。优先事项包括具有分类学意识的啮齿动物 监测、综合 One Health 预测、诊断 和转诊到提供体外膜氧合的中心,以及针对农村、土著和职业暴露社区的有针对性的预防。

title: A systematic review of mental health and neuropsychiatric outcomes among survivors of hantavirus infection
abstract: Hantavirus infections, including hantavirus cardiopulmonary syndrome (HCPS) and hemorrhagic fever with renal syndrome, can cause severe acute illness. Although survival has improved in some clinical settings, the mental health and neuropsychiatric outcomes associated with recovery remain insufficiently characterized. This systematic review synthesized the available evidence on mental health and neuropsychiatric outcomes associated with hantavirus infection, distinguishing persistent post-infectious symptoms from neurological complications occurring during acute illness. A systematic review was conducted with reference to PRISMA 2020 guidance. Electronic databases were searched for eligible studies published between 2005 and 2025. Methodological quality was evaluated using Joanna Briggs Institute appraisal tools, and findings were synthesized narratively because of substantial heterogeneity in study designs, populations, follow-up periods, and outcome assessment. Nine studies were included. Reported outcomes fell into two broad clinical categories. The first comprised persistent or follow-up symptoms, including fatigue, memory and concentration difficulties, psychological symptoms, sleep disturbances, and impaired quality of life. These outcomes were described in studies examining recovery after HCPS and Puumala virus-associated nephropathia epidemica. The second category comprised neurological complications, including encephalitis, altered mental status, and posterior reversible encephalopathy syndrome. These acute manifestations were interpreted separately from persistent post-infectious outcomes because their occurrence during acute illness does not establish long-term neuropsychiatric impairment. Differences in study design, sample size, follow-up duration, and outcome assessment limited direct comparisons and prevented reliable estimates of population-level prevalence. The available literature describes a range of persistent symptoms and acute neurological complications associated with hantavirus infection. However, the small and heterogeneous evidence base limits conclusions regarding their frequency, duration, mechanisms, and functional consequences. Larger longitudinal studies using standardized assessments and appropriate comparison groups are needed to clarify recovery trajectories and inform follow-up care.

elements_zh.scope_and_question: 本综述重点关注汉坦病毒感染幸存者的心理健康和神经精神结局,特别区分持续的感染后症状和急性疾病期间发生的神经系统并发症。核心问题是描述汉坦病毒感染后的长期心理健康和神经精神后遗症。
elements_zh.evidence_base_and_review_method: 根据 PRISMA 2020 指南进行了系统审查。我们在电子数据库中搜索了 2005 年至 2025 年间发表的符合条件的研究。使用乔安娜·布里格斯研究所评估工具评估方法学质量,由于研究设计、人群、随访期和结果评估存在显着异质性,结果以叙述方式综合。
elements_zh.consensus_and_key_conclusions: 现有文献描述了与汉坦病毒感染相关的一系列持续症状和急性神经并发症。这些后果包括疲劳、记忆力和注意力不集中、心理症状、睡眠障碍和生活质量受损,以及脑炎、精神状态改变和可逆性后部脑病综合征。然而,证据基础小且异构,限制了有关其频率、持续时间、机制和功能后果的结论。
elements_zh.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: 研究设计、样本量、随访持续时间和结果评估的差异限制了直接比较,并阻碍了对人群水平 患病率 的可靠估计。The heterogeneity in the evidence base also prevents drawing definitive conclusions about the long-term neuropsychiatric effects of汉坦病毒infection.
elements_zh.research_and_practice_implications: 需要使用标准化评估和适当的比较组进行更大规模的纵向研究,以阐明恢复轨迹并为后续护理提供信息。这将有助于更好地理解持续感染后症状和急性神经并发症的功能后果和机制。

title: One Health priorities beyond 2026: translating advances in science, surveillance and governance into prevention and preparedness.
abstract: The interdependence of human, animal and environmental health and persistent gaps between multisectoral commitments and effective implementation were highlighted in The Lancet 2023 One Health series. Since then, advances in genomic and environmental surveillance, artificial intelligence and international governance have created new opportunities for infectious disease prevention and preparedness. However, avian influenza A(H5N1), filovirus outbreaks, antimicrobial resistance and the 2026 Andes virus cruise-ship outbreak illustrate continuing challenges in surveillance, coordination and response. Climate-sensitive infections, foodborne zoonoses and environmental contamination further emphasize the need for integrated approaches extending beyond emerging viral threats. This review critically examines developments since 2023, distinguishing established preventive interventions from promising but incompletely validated technologies, and both proximate biosecurity controls and structural socio-ecological upstream prevention, from early detection and outbreak containment. We propose a six-stage surveillance-to-action pathway linking detection, verification, joint risk assessment, accountable decisions, coordinated interventions and double-loop evaluation. An operational matrix illustrates its application across emerging and endemic infections, antimicrobial resistance and environmental threats. Five priorities address interoperable participatory surveillance, evidence-based upstream prevention, integrated antimicrobial resistance action, sustainable national governance that redresses sectoral power asymmetries, and equitable regional capacity. Effective One Health implementation requires clear institutional responsibilities, sustained financing, co-designed community and indigenous participation and rigorous evaluation. Progress should ultimately be measured by demonstrable reductions in infectious disease risks and improved protection of human, animal and environmental health.

It explores the challenges in surveillance, coordination, and response to hantavirus-related diseases, including hemorrhagic fever with renal syndrome (HFRS) and hantavirus pulmonary syndrome (HPS). The central question is how to translate scientific and governance advances into effective prevention and preparedness measures for hantaviruses.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: The review is a critical analysis of developments since the 2023 One Health series, examining both established preventive interventions and emerging technologies. The review also outlines a six-stage surveillance-to-action pathway for integrating these approaches.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: The review concludes that effective One Health implementation is essential for reducing infectious disease risks, particularly for hantaviruses. The six-stage surveillance-to-action pathway is proposed as a framework for linking detection, verification, and coordinated interventions.
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: The review identifies gaps in surveillance systems, coordination between sectors, and the validation of new technologies for hantavirus prevention. It also highlights the challenges in addressing climate-sensitive infections and foodborne zoonoses, which require integrated approaches beyond the scope of hantavirus-specific interventions.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: The review proposes five priorities for research and practice: interoperable participatory surveillance, evidence-based upstream prevention, integrated antimicrobial resistance action, sustainable national governance that redresses sectoral power asymmetries, and equitable regional capacity. These priorities aim to improve the prevention and preparedness of hantavirus-related diseases.

It highlights the need for integrated approaches to address surveillance, coordination, and response gaps, particularly in the context of emerging viral threats like the 2026 Andes virus cruise-ship outbreak. The review proposes a six-stage surveillance-to-action pathway and five research and practice priorities to enhance prevention and preparedness. It underscores the importance of clear institutional roles, community participation, and sustainable governance in reducing infectious disease risks, including those associated with hantaviruses.

elements_zh.scope_and_question: 该审查的重点是实施“同一个健康”战略来解决 汉坦病毒,强调人类、动物和环境健康的相互依赖性。它探讨了 监测、协调和应对汉坦病毒相关疾病的挑战,包括 肾综合征出血热 (HFRS) 和 汉坦病毒肺综合征 (HPS)。核心问题是如何将科学和治理进步转化为有效的汉坦病毒预防和准备措施。
elements_zh.evidence_base_and_review_method: 该审查是对 2023 年“同一个健康”系列以来的发展的批判性分析,审查了既定的预防干预措施和新兴技术。它没有报告具体的数据库、搜索日期或研究计数,但强调了近似生物安全控制和结构性社会生态预防策略之间的区别。该评论还概述了整合这些方法的六阶段 监测 行动路径。
elements_zh.consensus_and_key_conclusions: 审查得出的结论是,有效实施“同一个健康”对于降低传染病风险至关重要,特别是对于汉坦病毒而言。它强调需要明确的机构责任、持续的融资和共同设计的社区参与。提出了六阶段 监测 行动路径作为连接检测、验证和协调干预的框架。
elements_zh.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: 该审查确定了 监测 系统、部门之间的协调以及汉坦病毒预防新技术的验证方面的差距。它还强调了解决气候敏感感染和食源性人畜共患病的挑战,这需要超越汉坦病毒特定干预措施范围的综合方法。
elements_zh.research_and_practice_implications: 该审查提出了研究和实践的五个优先事项:可互操作的参与性监测、基于证据的上游预防、综合抗菌素耐药性行动、纠正部门权力不对称的可持续国家治理以及公平的区域能力。这些优先事项旨在改善汉坦病毒相关疾病的预防和准备。

analysis_zh.scope_and_question: 该审查的重点是实施“同一个健康”战略来解决 汉坦病毒,强调人类、动物和环境健康的相互依赖性。它探讨了 监测、协调和应对汉坦病毒相关疾病的挑战,包括 肾综合征出血热 (HFRS) 和 汉坦病毒肺综合征 (HPS)。核心问题是如何将科学和治理进步转化为有效的汉坦病毒预防和准备措施。
analysis_zh.evidence_base_and_review_method: 该审查是对 2023 年“同一个健康”系列以来的发展的批判性分析,审查了既定的预防干预措施和新兴技术。它没有报告具体的数据库、搜索日期或研究计数,但强调了近似生物安全控制和结构性社会生态预防策略之间的区别。该评论还概述了整合这些方法的六阶段 监测 行动路径。
analysis_zh.consensus_and_key_conclusions: 审查得出的结论是,有效实施“同一个健康”对于降低传染病风险至关重要,特别是对于汉坦病毒而言。它强调需要明确的机构责任、持续的融资和共同设计的社区参与。提出了六阶段 监测 行动路径作为连接检测、验证和协调干预的框架。
analysis_zh.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: 该审查确定了 监测 系统、部门之间的协调以及汉坦病毒预防新技术的验证方面的差距。它还强调了解决气候敏感感染和食源性人畜共患病的挑战,这需要超越汉坦病毒特定干预措施范围的综合方法。
analysis_zh.research_and_practice_implications: 该审查提出了研究和实践的五个优先事项:可互操作的参与性监测、基于证据的上游预防、综合抗菌素耐药性行动、纠正部门权力不对称的可持续国家治理以及公平的区域能力。这些优先事项旨在改善汉坦病毒相关疾病的预防和准备。

title: Codon usage patterns of heartland virus show segment-specific variation and greater similarity to human than to tick codon usage
abstract: Introduction Heartland virus (HRTV) is an emerging tick‐borne pathogen causing severe human illness. The evolutionary factors shaping its codon usage and host adaptation remain poorly understood. Methods We analyzed HRTV codon‐usage patterns using 69 non‐redundant coding sequences (CDSs) derived from 65 HRTV segment records in GenBank. Analyses included ENc‐GC3s, parity rule 2 (PR2), neutrality regression, host‐reference codon‐usage indices, phylogeny, and statistical testing. Results HRTV showed low‐to‐moderate codon‐usage bias with marked segment‐specific variation. ENc‐GC3s and PR2 revealed deviations from mutation‐only expectations, pointing to non‐mutational influences. Neutrality regressions were non‐significant and could not quantify contributions from natural selection, genetic drift, or RNA structural constraints. HRTV codon usage was most similar to Homo sapiens and least similar to Haemaphysalis longicornis. Consistently elevated RCDI values (>1) highlighted the descriptive nature of these indices. Phylogeny‐integrated statistics showed CAI differences across phylogenetic clades and, for the M segment, across geographic regions, while no significant host‐specific differences were found for any segment, including NP and NSs of the ambisense S segment. Discussion Given geographic sampling biases and humans being only incidental hosts, these findings offer a descriptive framework for interpreting HRTV codon‐usage patterns rather than definitive evidence of host adaptation.

title: Broad-spectrum antiviral database (BSA-DB): a curated collection of broad-spectrum antiviral agents assembled by large language model mining and expert curation
abstract: Viruses included in the World Health Organization R&D Blueprint priority list pose a continuing epidemic and pandemic threat, highlighting the need for rapidly deployable antiviral discovery resources. Broad-spectrum antivirals (BSAs), which are active against multiple viruses, represent promising starting points for pandemic preparedness, yet relevant bioactivity data remain fragmented across public databases. Here we present BSA-DB, a freely accessible resource comprising 13,194 compounds with reported activity ≤ 10000 nM against at least two of 22 Blueprint viruses spanning 10 virus families (initially 23 viruses were selected, but Hantaan virus yielded no compounds meeting this criterion). BSA-DB was obtained from ChEMBL, PubChem and BindingDB, followed by systematic data curation and standardization of viral annotations. Cheminformatic analysis shows that the collection is chemically diverse rather than dominated by a few known antiviral chemotypes, and identifies recurrent scaffolds, structural clusters with broad virus coverage, and promising starting points for antiviral drug discovery. BSA-DB is available at https://bsadb.denovosciences.ai/through an interactive web platform with search, filtering, visualization and bulk-download functionality, and will be continuously expanded with newly available and community-contributed data.

title_zh: 广谱抗病毒药物数据库(BSA-DB):由大型语言模型挖掘和专家管理组装而成的广谱抗病毒药物代理的精选集合
source_body_en: Viruses included in the World Health Organization R&D Blueprint priority list pose a continuing epidemic and pandemic threat, highlighting the need for rapidly deployable antiviral discovery resources. Broad-spectrum antivirals (BSAs), which are active against multiple viruses, represent promising starting points for pandemic preparedness, yet relevant bioactivity data remain fragmented across public databases. Here we present BSA-DB, a freely accessible resource comprising 13,194 compounds with reported activity ≤ 10000 nM against at least two of 22 Blueprint viruses spanning 10 virus families (initially 23 viruses were selected, but Hantaan virus yielded no compounds meeting this criterion). BSA-DB was obtained from ChEMBL, PubChem and BindingDB, followed by systematic data curation and standardization of viral annotations. Cheminformatic analysis shows that the collection is chemically diverse rather than dominated by a few known antiviral chemotypes, and identifies recurrent scaffolds, structural clusters with broad virus coverage, and promising starting points for antiviral drug discovery. BSA-DB is available at https://bsadb.denovosciences.ai/through an interactive web platform with search, filtering, visualization and bulk-download functionality, and will be continuously expanded with newly available and community-contributed data.

full_text: Abstract Host classification from viral genomic sequences is challenging because biologically meaningful signals must be extracted from high-dimensional sequence data under strong class imbalance. This paper presents a hybrid quantum machine learning framework for binary human versus non-human host classification. Raw nucleotide sequences are first encoded using a frozen DNABERT-2 model and compressed into bounded low-dimensional latent vectors through a bottleneck autoencoder. These quantum-compatible features are then classified using the proposed Segment-Aware Entangled Quantum Classifier (SEQC), a compact variational quantum decision module with trainable dual-angle encoding, data re-uploading, segment-aware local-to-global entanglement, global mixing, and trainable observable readout. Experiments are conducted in a leakage-safe, resource-controlled simulation setting: classifier training uses a balanced subset of samples, while validation, threshold tuning, and testing are performed on the full natural imbalanced splits. On the natural test set, SEQC achieves \(0.8833\) accuracy, \(0.7224\) balanced accuracy, \(0.7243\) macro-F1, \(0.7740\) ROC-AUC, and \(0.5167\) minority-class PR-AUC using only \(138\) trainable classifier parameters. Comparisons with classical baselines show that SEQC is competitive as a compact nonlinear decision module, particularly in minority-class ranking. Ablation studies further indicate that encoding choice, bottleneck dimension, and entanglement structure should be matched to the supplied latent representation. title_original: Segment-Aware Entangled Quantum Classifier for Imbalanced Hantavirus Host Prediction

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to address the challenge of host classification from viral genomic sequences, particularly in the context of imbalanced data, which is critical for understanding hantavirus transmission and pathogenesis.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study presents a hybrid quantum machine learning framework for binary human versus non-human host classification, using a balanced subset of samples for training and full natural imbalanced splits for validation, threshold tuning, and testing.
analysis.methods: Raw nucleotide sequences are encoded using a frozen DNABERT-2 model and compressed into low-dimensional latent vectors through a bottleneck autoencoder. These quantum-compatible features are then classified using the Segment-Aware Entangled Quantum Classifier (SEQC), which incorporates trainable dual-angle encoding, data re-uploading, segment-aware local-to-global entanglement, global mixing, and trainable observable readout.
analysis.main_results: On the natural test set, SEQC achieved 0.8833 accuracy, 0.7224 balanced accuracy, 0.7243 macro-F1, 0.7740 ROC-AUC, and 0.5167 minority-class PR-AUC using only 138 trainable classifier parameters.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpret that SEQC is competitive as a compact nonlinear decision module, particularly in minority-class ranking, and highlight its novelty as a framework tailored for imbalanced data in host prediction.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings can inform the development of more accurate and efficient methods for predicting hantavirus hosts, which is crucial for surveillance, risk assessment, and prevention strategies in public health.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited to a simulation setting, and the evidence strength is moderate due to the absence of real-world validation and potential generalizability issues.

analysis.summary_en: This study introduces a hybrid quantum machine learning framework called the Segment-Aware Entangled Quantum Classifier (SEQC) for predicting hantavirus hosts from genomic sequences. The research addresses the challenge of extracting biologically meaningful signals from high-dimensional and imbalanced sequence data, which is essential for understanding hantavirus transmission and pathogenesis. The framework uses a frozen DNABERT-2 model to encode raw nucleotide sequences and compresses them into low-dimensional latent vectors via a bottleneck autoencoder. These features are then classified using SEQC, which incorporates quantum-compatible techniques such as trainable dual-angle encoding, data re-uploading, and segment-aware entanglement. On the natural test set, SEQC achieved 0.8833 accuracy, 0.7224 balanced accuracy, 0.7243 macro-F1, 0.7740 ROC-AUC, and 0.5167 minority-class PR-AUC using only 138 trainable parameters. The authors interpret that SEQC is competitive in minority-class ranking, offering a novel approach for imbalanced data in host prediction. The findings have implications for improving surveillance and risk assessment for hantavirus infections. However, the study is limited to a simulation setting, which may affect its generalizability and real-world applicability.

elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 该研究提出了一种混合量子机器学习框架,用于人类与非人类 宿主 分类,使用平衡的样本子集进行训练,并使用完全自然的不平衡分割进行验证、阈值调整和测试。
elements_zh.methods: 原始核苷酸序列使用冷冻 DNABERT-2 模型进行编码,并通过瓶颈自动编码器压缩为低维潜在 媒介。然后使用分段感知纠缠量子分类器 (SEQC) 对这些量子兼容特征进行分类,该分类器结合了可训练的双角度编码、数据重新上传、分段感知的局部到全局纠缠、全局混合和可训练的可观察读数。
elements_zh.main_results: 在自然测试集上,SEQC 仅使用 138 个可训练分类器参数就实现了 0.8833 准确率、0.7224 平衡准确率、0.7243 宏 F1、0.7740 ROC-AUC 和 0.5167 少数类 PR-AUC。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 作者解释说,SEQC 作为紧凑的非线性决策模块具有竞争力,特别是在少数群体排名中,并强调了它作为针对 宿主 预测中不平衡数据量身定制的框架的新颖性。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些发现可以为开发更准确、更有效的方法来预测汉坦病毒宿主 提供信息,这对于公共卫生领域的 监测、风险评估和预防策略至关重要。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究仅限于模拟环境,由于缺乏现实世界的验证和潜在的普遍性问题,证据强度中等。

full_text: Abstract Hantavirus infection can lead to hemorrhagic fever with renal syndrome and hantavirus cardiopulmonary syndrome, and cardiovascular (CV) involvement is increasingly recognized as an important feature of severe disease. The present review summarizes the epidemiology, clinical manifestations, pathophysiological mechanisms, diagnostic evaluation, and management of CV involvement in hantavirus infection. The available evidence includes experimental studies, observational cohorts, case series, and clinical reports. Reported CV manifestations include myocardial injury, myocarditis, ventricular dysfunction, cardiogenic shock, pericardial involvement, conduction abnormalities, and atrial or ventricular arrhythmias. Proposed mechanisms include endothelial dysfunction, increased vascular permeability, inflammatory and cytokine activation, autonomic nervous system dysregulation, and microvascular abnormalities. Clinical assessment may reveal hypotension, elevated cardiac biomarkers, ventricular dysfunction, and circulatory collapse. Echocardiography, cardiac biomarker assessment, electrocardiography, speckle-tracking echocardiography, and cardiac magnetic resonance imaging may aid diagnosis and risk stratification. Management is largely supportive and may include individualized fluid management, vasopressors and inotropes as needed, hemodynamic monitoring, and mechanical circulatory support or extracorporeal membrane oxygenation for refractory shock. The current evidence base is limited by the predominance of observational data and heterogeneity in diagnostic and follow-up strategies. Prospective studies are needed to clarify the mechanisms of myocardial injury, identify prognostic biomarkers, and establish evidence-based approaches to CV assessment and management. Keywords: Arrhythmia, capillary leak syndrome, cardiogenic shock, endothelial dysfunction, myocarditis INTRODUCTION Hantaviruses are zoonotic, enveloped viruses with negative-sense, single-stranded RNA genomes belonging to the family Hantaviridae. Rodents serve as their natural reservoirs, and humans become infected by inhaling aerosols containing infected rodent excreta. Hantavirus infections are a global public health concern and can cause severe disease. Their geographic distribution is closely associated with the distribution of their reservoir species. In Europe and Asia, hantavirus infections typically manifest as hemorrhagic fever with renal syndrome (HFRS), whereas in the Americas, the most common presentation is hantavirus cardiopulmonary syndrome (HCPS). HFRS is characterized by fever, thrombocytopenia, vascular leakage, and renal failure, whereas HCPS is primarily associated with pulmonary edema, respiratory failure, and circulatory collapse. Despite differences in their clinical presentations, both syndromes are associated with increased vascular permeability and endothelial dysfunction.1-3 Research on hantavirus infection has traditionally focused on its pulmonary and renal manifestations. However, accumulating evidence suggests that cardiovascular (CV) involvement may also contribute to disease severity and clinical outcomes. Reported CV manifestations range from mild myocardial injury and hemodynamic abnormalities to myocarditis, ventricular dysfunction, arrhythmias, cardiogenic shock, and, rarely, sudden cardiac death. The CV effects of hantavirus infection may involve endothelial activation, capillary leakage, systemic inflammation, and hemodynamic disturbances. Nevertheless, the mechanisms underlying CV involvement and the extent to which individual mechanisms contribute to clinical outcomes remain poorly understood. Accordingly, this review examines the pathophysiological mechanisms, clinical manifestations, diagnostic approaches, and therapeutic implications of hantavirus-associated CV involvement.4-6 Citation Strategy Citations were reassessed throughout the manuscript to improve the alignment between individual statements and their supporting sources. Hantavirus-specific and CV references were prioritized for claims concerning CV manifestations, myocardial injury, hemodynamic abnormalities, imaging, biomarkers, and clinical outcomes. Broader reviews and general critical care or CV sources were retained primarily to support general concepts and management principles when hantavirus-specific evidence was limited. Duplicate citations were reduced where appropriate, and citation placement was reviewed to ensure that each reference supports the corresponding statement. Literature Review Methodology This article is a narrative review. The relevant literature was identified through a focused search of the biomedical literature using combinations of the following terms: “hantavirus,” “hantavirus infection,” “hemorrhagic fever with renal syndrome,” “hantavirus cardiopulmonary syndrome,” “cardiovascular,” “cardiac,” “myocarditis,” “heart failure,” “shock,” “arrhythmia,” “echocardiography,” “speckle-tracking echocardiography,” “cardiac magnetic resonance,” “biomarkers,” and “extracorporeal membrane oxygenation.” Original research articles, observational studies, case series, case reports, reviews, and guideline or consensus documents were considered based on their relevance to the CV manifestations, mechanisms of injury, diagnostic evaluation, management, and long-term outcomes of hantavirus infection. The reference lists of relevant publications were also screened to identify additional studies. Because this was a narrative review, no formal systematic review protocol, meta-analysis, or quantitative risk-of-bias assessment was undertaken. The available evidence was critically appraised, with particular attention to the predominantly observational nature of the published literature and the methodological heterogeneity among studies. Host and Viral Responses Hantaviruses are enveloped viruses with negative-sense, single-stranded RNA genomes belonging to the family Hantaviridae. Hantavirus genomes are tripartite and consist of three segments (S, M, and L) that encode the nucleocapsid protein, the envelope glycoproteins (Gn and Gc), and the RNA-dependent RNA polymerase. The envelope glycoproteins are involved in viral attachment to and entry into host cells, whereas the nucleocapsid protein plays a role in viral replication and interactions with host immune responses. Hantaviruses are transmitted by rodents, with each viral species typically associated with a specific rodent reservoir. Infected animals may shed the virus in their urine, feces, and saliva, resulting in environmental contamination and subsequent aerosol transmission to humans. South American hantavirus strains are associated with HCPS, and person-to-person transmission has been reported for some strains.7,8 Hantavirus glycoproteins interact with β3 integrins expressed on endothelial and other vascular cells, platelets, and additional cell types. Following receptor-mediated entry, viral replication takes place in the cytoplasm. Endothelial involvement is associated with increased vascular permeability and capillary leakage, both of which are prominent features of severe disease. Available evidence suggests that host immune responses are major determinants of disease severity. Although hantaviruses are generally considered non-cytopathic, infection can activate T-cells, macrophages, and natural killer cells. Endothelial dysfunction and increased vascular permeability have been associated with inflammatory mediators, including tumor necrosis factor-α (TNF-α), interleukin (IL)-6, and interferon-γ. Severe hantavirus infection may therefore be accompanied by cardiac and hemodynamic abnormalities, although the relative contributions of immune-mediated mechanisms remain incompletely understood.9,10 Pathophysiology of CV Injury CV involvement in hantavirus infection likely results from interactions among viral infection, endothelial dysfunction, immune dysregulation, and hemodynamic disturbances. Experimental and pathological observations suggest that hantaviruses predominantly affect vascular endothelial cells rather than cardiomyocytes. Systemic inflammatory responses have also been reported. Together, these processes have been proposed to contribute to ventricular dysfunction, arrhythmias, circulatory collapse, and multiorgan dysfunction.11 Endothelial Dysfunction Endothelial dysfunction is a well-recognized feature of severe hantavirus infection. The effects of viral particles on endothelial cells may be mediated through mechanisms that are not directly related to cytolysis. Endothelial dysregulation may lead to the disruption of intercellular junctions, increased vascular permeability, and impaired regulation of vascular tone. Experimental studies show that hantavirus glycoproteins bind to β3 integrins and disrupt endothelial signaling and barrier function. Endothelial barrier dysfunction has also been linked to permeability mediators such as vascular endothelial growth factor and angiopoietins. These pathological changes may cause hypotension, tissue edema, and reduced organ perfusion.12 Capillary Leak Syndrome Severe hantavirus infection is characterized by CV instability and capillary leak syndrome. Increased endothelial permeability allows proteins and fluid to extravasate into the interstitial space, causing tissue edema and intravascular volume depletion. In HCPS, pulmonary capillary leakage may lead to pulmonary edema and profound hypoxia. Reduced effective intravascular volume may also cause hypotension and shock secondary to reduced cardiac preload. Severe capillary leakage may further impair ventricular filling and oxygen delivery to myocardial cells, thereby contributing to reduced ventricular function. The extent of vascular leakage has been associated with adverse clinical outcomes.13 Cytokine Activation and Inflammation Inflammatory pathways are considered important contributors to CV involvement in hantavirus infection. Proinflammatory cytokines, such as TNF-α, IL-1β, IL-6, IL-8, and interferon-γ, have been reported in clinical and experimental studies. The upregulation of these cytokines has been associated with increased endothelial permeability, leukocyte recruitment, and vascular inflammation. Inflammatory mediators may also exert negative inotropic effects. For example, TNF-α and IL-6 have been associated with abnormalities in calcium handling, reduced myocardial contractility, and mitochondrial dysfunction. Transient myocardial dysfunction has been reported in severe hantavirus infection, and cytokine-mediated myocardial depression has been proposed as one of the mechanisms contributing to this finding.14 Pathogenesis of Myocardial Injury Myocardial injury in hantavirus infection likely has a multifactorial etiology. Current evidence suggests that immune-mediated and endothelial mechanisms may contribute to myocardial injury, whereas the extent of direct cardiomyocyte infection remains uncertain. Myocarditis has not been characterized in detail in patients with hantavirus infection. However, clinicopathological findings suggestive of myocarditis have been reported in some cases, along with ventricular dysfunction and elevated cardiac troponin levels. Cytokines are thought to contribute to myocardial depression, although microvascular dysfunction, systemic hypoperfusion, oxidative stress, and inflammatory cell infiltration may also play a role. These processes may lead to myocardial dysfunction, myocarditis, and cardiogenic shock in susceptible patients. The recovery of ventricular function reported in many cases suggests that reversible functional impairment may predominate over irreversible myocyte injury in at least some patients.15 The proposed pathophysiological mechanisms linking hantavirus infection to CV injury and their potential clinical consequences are illustrated in . Microvascular Dysfunction Microvascular dysfunction has been proposed as an additional mechanism contributing to CV involvement in hantavirus infection. Microcirculatory blood flow may be compromised by endothelial and complement activation, inflammatory cytokines, and coagulopathy. Increased vascular permeability and interstitial edema may increase the diffusion distance for oxygen, while platelet activation and local thrombus formation may further impair microvascular perfusion. These abnormalities may impair myocardial perfusion even in the presence of minimal epicardial coronary artery disease. Microvascular dysfunction has therefore been proposed as a potential contributor to myocardial ischemia, ventricular dysfunction, arrhythmias, and hemodynamic deterioration. Systemic microcirculatory impairment may also contribute to multiorgan dysfunction. However, the relative importance of these mechanisms and their prognostic significance in hantavirus infection remain incompletely established.16 The pathophysiological processes outlined above-including endothelial dysfunction, capillary leakage, systemic inflammation, myocardial injury, and microvascular abnormalities-provide a plausible basis for the range of CV manifestations reported in hantavirus infection. These processes may manifest clinically as transient hemodynamic disturbances, subclinical myocardial injury, overt ventricular dysfunction, myocarditis, arrhythmias, or cardiogenic shock. Understanding the links between these underlying mechanisms and their clinical consequences is important for recognizing and managing CV involvement. The next section therefore examines the principal CV manifestations reported in patients with hantavirus infection.16 CV Manifestations CV manifestations are increasingly recognized as contributors to morbidity and mortality in hantavirus infection. Although pulmonary and renal complications have been studied more extensively, CV involvement is an important feature of severe HCPS. The clinical spectrum ranges from mild hemodynamic abnormalities to severe ventricular dysfunction and circulatory collapse. Endothelial dysfunction, increased vascular permeability, systemic inflammation, and myocardial injury have been implicated in the CV manifestations of severe disease.17 Shock and Hypotension Hypotension is a common CV manifestation of severe hantavirus infection. Inflammatory mediators induce vasodilation, leading to decreased systemic vascular resistance, while increased vascular permeability causes plasma leakage into the tissues and reduces effective intravascular volume. Consequently, shock may be hypovolemic, distributive, cardiogenic, or mixed. In patients with significant myocardial dysfunction, fluid therapy may exacerbate pulmonary edema and hemodynamic instability. Persistent hypotension should prompt a comprehensive hemodynamic evaluation and the initiation of vasopressor support, as indicated.18 Myocarditis Myocarditis has been reported in patients with HFRS and HCPS, although its frequency and clinical significance remain uncertain. Clinical features have included chest pain, electrocardiographic changes, elevated cardiac biomarkers, and reversible ventricular dysfunction. Histopathological analyses have revealed interstitial inflammatory infiltrates, myocardial edema, and focal myocyte injury. In patients with suspected myocarditis, cardiac magnetic resonance (CMR) imaging may demonstrate myocardial edema and late gadolinium enhancement. Immune-mediated mechanisms and cytokine-associated myocardial depression have been proposed, although direct viral injury to the myocardium cannot be excluded. Ventricular function appears to recover in many patients after the acute illness.15 Pericardial Involvement Pericardial involvement appears to be less common than myocardial dysfunction but has been reported in patients with hantavirus infection. Acute pericarditis may present with chest pain and electrocardiographic changes, whereas echocardiography may reveal a small pericardial effusion. Pericardial abnormalities may develop in the setting of systemic inflammation and increased vascular permeability. Although clinically significant cardiac tamponade appears to be rare, hemodynamic deterioration should prompt echocardiographic assessment. Echocardiography is useful for diagnosing and monitoring pericardial involvement.19,20 Acute Heart Failure Severe hantavirus infection may be complicated by acute heart failure. Rapid-onset ventricular dysfunction has been associated with myocardial inflammation, cytokine-mediated myocardial depression, microvascular abnormalities, and acute changes in ventricular loading conditions. Clinical features may include dyspnea, pulmonary congestion, elevated natriuretic peptide concentrations, and reduced left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF). In HCPS, acute ventricular dysfunction may contribute to pulmonary edema and complicate the differentiation of cardiogenic from non-cardiogenic respiratory failure. In some patients, transient inflammatory and hemodynamic disturbances may play a greater role than irreversible structural myocardial damage.15 Right Ventricular Dysfunction Right ventricular dysfunction may be underrecognized in severe hantavirus infection. Pulmonary edema, hypoxic pulmonary vasoconstriction, and pulmonary vascular abnormalities may increase right ventricular afterload. Echocardiography in critically ill patients may reveal right ventricular enlargement associated with impaired function or elevated pulmonary artery pressure. Because right ventricular function is essential for maintaining cardiac output, significant right ventricular dysfunction may contribute to hemodynamic deterioration. A comprehensive echocardiographic examination should therefore include an assessment of right ventricular size and systolic function.21 Cardiogenic Shock Cardiogenic shock is a severe manifestation of CV involvement in HCPS and has been associated with high mortality in reported cohorts. It highlights the clinical manifestations such as myocardial injury, myocarditis, and cardiogenic shock, as well as proposed mechanisms like endothelial dysfunction and vascular permeability. analysis_zh.research_question_and_background: 随着心血管受累越来越被认为是严重疾病的一个重要特征,本综述旨在总结 流行病学 感染中心血管受累的 流行病学、临床表现、病理生理机制、诊断评估和处理。
analysis_zh.study_design_and_population: 该研究是对现有证据的回顾,其中包括实验研究、观察性 队列研究、病例系列和临床报告。它涵盖了人类汉坦病毒感染,特别关注心血管表现。
analysis_zh.methods: 该综述综合了来自实验研究、观察性 队列研究、病例系列和临床报告的数据,这些数据用于识别报告的心血管表现和提出的疾病机制。
analysis_zh.main_results: 报道的心血管表现包括心肌损伤、心肌炎、心室功能障碍、心源性休克、心包受累、传导异常以及房性或室性心律失常。提出的机制包括内皮功能障碍、血管通透性增加、炎症和细胞因子激活、自主神经系统失调和微血管异常。
analysis_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 作者解释说,心血管受累可能会导致疾病的严重程度和临床结果,强调需要进一步研究以阐明机制并改进管理策略。
analysis_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些发现可能有助于开发更准确的诊断工具和针对汉坦病毒感染心血管并发症的有针对性的管理方法,这是一个全球公共卫生问题。
analysis_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 证据受到观察数据的主导以及诊断和随访策略的异质性的限制,这可能会影响研究结果的普遍性。证据强度中等。

full_text: nature immunology Volume 27 | December 2026 | 2357–2359 | 2357 Vaccine preparedness for the next emerging infectious disease crisis Florian Krammer Recent outbreaks with viruses such as Bundi­bugyo virus and Andes virus are a reminder that another pandemic can happen at any time. This Comment summarizes where we stand with pandemic preparedness from a vaccine perspective. During the COVID-19 pandemic, we witnessed vaccine develop­ment at its finest. Vaccines against the novel coronavirus SARS-CoV-2 were developed at record speed and were made available within approximately 1 year after the outbreak started1. This swift devel­ opment of vaccines was facilitated by new technologies such as the mRNA vaccine platform2 but also by a wealth of exist­ ing knowledge because of many years of virology, vacci­nology and structural biology research. Much has happened since the COVID-19 pandemic. Technology has evolved, new insights into mechanisms of protection and basic immunology have been gained and regulatory and policy views have changed (Fig. 1), especially in the USA. Where does this leave us with vaccine preparedness for emerging pathogens? Mucosal immunity matters A clear lesson learned from the COVID-19 pandemic was that intramus­ cular vaccination can only imperfectly protect from infection with respiratory viruses per se and from onward transmission1. Vaccines that are administered via mucosal surfaces may be a better option to induce immunity in the upper respiratory tract to protect from infection with respiratory viruses. This was clearly identified as a gap, and funding agencies, including the US National Institute of Allergy and Infectious Diseases (NIAID) and Biomedical Advanced Research and Development Authority (BARDA), set out to support the development of mucosal vaccine approaches for COVID-19 (ref. 3). Unfortunately, funding for many of these vaccines was terminated or redirected to other projects owing to the policy decision that COVID-19 is no longer a priority. How­ ever, having infection- and transmission-blocking vaccines early in an outbreak with a respiratory virus would notably increase the effect of vaccines. Although several intranasal vaccines for COVID-19 are either still in development or already licensed outside the USA and Europe4,5, there is a large gap in terms of vaccine preparedness when it comes to mucosal vaccination routes. Having mucosal vaccines with clear immunological (and potentially mucosal) correlates of protection and established vaccine efficacy and safety on the market would increase confidence in these vaccine platforms and would likely enable early deployment during an outbreak or a pandemic. Broadly protective or strain-specific vaccines Studies of influenza virus and HIV-1 have shown that RNA viruses can evolve quickly. This was also observed with SARS-CoV-2. With the emergence of the Omicron variants, vaccines had to be updated to stay effective. However, updating vaccines to respond to emerging variants means always being one step behind the virus. This is a scenario with which we are very familiar from influenza virus vaccines. Owing to the antigenic variability of RNA viruses, the development of broadly protective vaccines has been the focus in the HIV-1 and influenza fields for many years but also became an important topic for SARS-CoV-2. The concept of broadly protective vaccines goes further than the idea of covering evolving virus variants. The idea has expanded to develop vaccines that potentially can protect from whole virus families, which would considerably increase pandemic preparedness. Although fund­ ing for such vaccines has been made available (for example, via the NIAID Collaborative Influenza Vaccine Innovation Centers program, the BARDA funding initiatives and the European Health and Digital Executive Agency), they have not progressed far enough to be used in case of an emergency. Further investment is urgently needed to advance these candidates and concepts through clinical development and real­ ize their potential as tools to combat evolving viral threats and future Comment https://doi.org/10.1038/s41590-026-02726-w Check for updates Broadly protective vs virus/strain- specific vaccines Mucosal vs injected vaccines Vaccine platform Vaccine acceptance Market Regulatory policy Manufacturing speed Funding policy Basic research Vaccine preparedness Vaccine Fig. 1 | Factors and aspects that influence epidemic and pandemic vaccine preparedness. Although technology has advanced, questions about broadly protective versus specific vaccines and mucosal vaccines remain. In addition, recent changes in funding and regulatory policy increase uncertainty for vaccine preparedness. nature immunology Volume 27 | December 2026 | 2357–2359 | 2358 Comment pandemics. In addition, the regulatory pathway to get such vaccines licensed remains unclear. Vaccines need to be tested in phase 3 efficacy trials to show how well they protect against disease. To demonstrate that a vaccine is broadly protective, multi-year trials to show efficacy in seasons with antigenic changes are likely needed, and such trials may be prohibitively expensive. Furthermore, demonstrating efficacy against pathogens that are not yet circulating in humans is impossible, making it difficult to claim universal protection against future pathogens with pandemic potential. For pandemic preparedness, strain-matched vac­ cines that can be generated rapidly after the emergence of a new virus currently seems to be favored over the development of broadly protec­ tive vaccines (for example, https://cepi.net/100-days). Although this is of course also a good approach, it would be better to have vaccines ready before a new outbreak even starts and not months later, which is something that a broadly protective or universal vaccine could deliver. Pandemic influenza breakthroughs The recent pan-zootic with highly pathogenic H5N1 clade 2.3.4.4b influenza virus and its spillover into many mammalian species has raised concerns about the potential of this virus to cause a pandemic6. Fortunately, recent developments have enhanced pandemic influenza vaccine preparedness. For influenza vaccines, a correlate of protection accepted by regulators exists — the hemagglutination inhibition titer — although several other validated correlates of protection have also been established by academic researchers7. If a vaccine manufacturer has a licensed seasonal influenza virus vaccine on the market, the same technology can be used to manufacture a vaccine for an emerging pandemic influenza virus strain and get it to the market based on this correlate, instead of performing time-consuming phase 3 field efficacy trials first. Although effectiveness must be confirmed later, this step saves a lot of time during an outbreak. So far, this pathway has been open to manufacturers who are producing influenza vaccines using traditional technologies, such as split-inactivated vaccines. To update these vaccines to a new pandemic strain can be time-consuming. This process can be faster using the mRNA platform, but until recently, no mRNA-based seasonal influenza vaccines were available, meaning that this quick strain-change pathway was not open to the mRNA technol­ ogy. The recent licensure of an mRNA-based seasonal influenza vaccine from Moderna (mFLUSIVA in the USA; mCOMBRIAX in the European Union) changed this8. Although the benefits of an mRNA-based sea­ sonal influenza vaccine compared with conventional vaccines remain debated, the advantage in terms of speed in case of a pandemic is a game changer. Using the mechanism of a strain change from seasonal strains to a pandemic strain in combination with the mRNA technology may make it possible to have a matched pandemic influenza vaccine ready for use in the population within 3 months. The Bundibugyo virus outbreak as a test In May 2026, an outbreak with Bundibugyo virus was reported in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC)9. This outbreak is still ongo­ ing, case numbers are growing and it has now become the second larg­ est outbreak of Ebola disease in recorded history. Although vaccines against another virus species, Ebola virus (formerly known as Zaire ebolavirus), are licensed and available, strain-matched vaccines for Bundibugyo virus had not been clinically developed10. This crisis in the DRC serves as test for post-COVID-19 pandemic vaccine preparedness. So far, two vaccines have moved into clinical evaluation. The first phase 1 trial, based on an adenovirus vector (ChAdOx1-BDBV-GP), began in July in the UK11. A second trial, with an mRNA vaccine, was initiated in August in Canada (mRNA-1469, ClinicalTrials.gov NCT07737717). How long it takes to move these vaccines forward in the clinical pipeline, whether they are successful, and if they are fast enough to be used in the current outbreak remain to be determined. It is, however, notewor­ thy that these two vaccines are based on the same technologies that delivered the first COVID-19 vaccines. The value of basic research for vaccine preparedness Another aspect that needs to be mentioned is basic research that is being conducted to better understand emerging viruses that have so far gained little interest, especially viruses belonging to the Bunyaviri­ cetes. This class includes viruses such as severe fever with thrombocy­ topenia syndrome virus (SFTSV), Crimean-Congo hemorrhagic fever virus (CCHVF), Toscana virus (TOSV), Heartland virus, Shamonda virus, Yezo virus12 and Asian longhorned tick nairovirus (ALTNV)13, as well as hantaviruses such as Andes virus14. Some of these viruses are already human-to-human transmissible and have caused concerning outbreaks, such as the Andes virus outbreak in May on the cruise ship MV Hondius15. The spike proteins of these viruses were not well understood, making vaccine design complicated. Recent advances in understanding the molecular biology, structural biology and antigenicity of these viruses, partially funded by the excellent NIAID Research and Development of Vaccines and Monoclonal Antibodies for Pandemic Preparedness (ReVAMPP) program, have started to change that. Using new technolo­ gies and insights, vaccines against these challenging targets can now potentially also be developed quickly if needed, highlighting the need for and value of basic research. Conclusions The obvious question is, are we now, after the COVID-19 pandemic, better prepared for coming epidemics and pandemics in respect to vac­ cines? The answer is not a simple yes or no. Technology has advanced, our understanding of virus biology has markedly increased and COVID- 19 has shown us that vaccines can be developed quickly if needed and if an effort is made by all stakeholders. However, there is much still to learn; from basic research and clinical testing to manufacturing and regulatory policies. Importantly, funding policies and regulatory policies are changing in parts of the world, partially influenced by the anti-vaccine movement that now has advocates within governments. It is unclear what the long-term effect of these changes is on vaccine development and pandemic preparedness. analysis.research_question_and_background: The study addresses the need for improved vaccine preparedness against emerging infectious diseases, particularly highlighting the importance of mucosal immunity in protecting against respiratory viruses. The background emphasizes the lessons learned from the COVID-19 pandemic, where intramuscular vaccination had limited effectiveness in preventing infection and transmission.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study is a commentary that summarizes the current state of pandemic preparedness from a vaccine development perspective. It discusses the evolution of vaccine technologies, insights into immunological mechanisms, and changes in regulatory and policy approaches since the COVID-19 pandemic, with a focus on respiratory viruses.
analysis.methods: The methods section is not explicitly detailed in the provided evidence, but the commentary outlines the use of new technologies such as mRNA platforms and references studies on influenza virus and HIV-1 to highlight the challenges of developing broadly protective or strain-specific vaccines for RNA viruses.
analysis.main_results: The main results include the observation that intramuscular vaccination only imperfectly protects against respiratory virus infection and transmission. It also notes that several intranasal vaccines for COVID-19 are either in development or licensed outside the USA and Europe, but there remains a significant gap in mucosal vaccine preparedness.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpret that mucosal vaccines could offer better protection against respiratory viruses, especially if they have clear immunological correlates of protection and established efficacy and safety. This interpretation is novel in its emphasis on the potential of mucosal vaccination routes for future pandemic preparedness.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings suggest that developing mucosal vaccines with proven immunological correlates could enhance preparedness for future respiratory virus outbreaks, allowing for more effective early deployment and potentially reducing the spread of infection.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is a commentary and does not present original data, which limits its evidence strength. However, it draws on existing knowledge and references to provide a high-level overview of current vaccine preparedness challenges and opportunities.

analysis.summary_en: This commentary discusses the importance of mucosal immunity in protecting against respiratory viruses, highlighting the limitations of intramuscular vaccination observed during the COVID-19 pandemic. It emphasizes the need for mucosal vaccines with clear immunological correlates of protection and established efficacy and safety. The study also notes that while several intranasal vaccines for COVID-19 are in development or licensed outside the USA and Europe, there remains a significant gap in mucosal vaccine preparedness. The findings suggest that such vaccines could improve pandemic preparedness by enabling early deployment and reducing transmission. However, the commentary lacks original data and is based on existing knowledge, which limits its evidence strength.

full_text: nature immunology Volume 27 | December 2026 | 2363–2365 | 2363 The European Vaccines Hub Rino Rappuoli, Isabelle Bekeredjian-Ding, Pierre Van Damme, James P. Di Santo, Donata Medaglini & Michel Pletschette The European Vaccines Hub is a novel design consortium that assembles leading European organizations involved in vaccine development. The mission is to develop vaccines and monoclonal antibodies ensuring Europe’s pandemics and emerging infections readiness. When the COVID-19 pandemic struck the European Union, it was insufficiently prepared to face the devastating health and economic emergency. Although European biotech contributed significantly to the development of vaccines with products such as Comirnaty, the mRNA vaccine developed by the German BioNTech was eventually licensed to and commercialized by an American company, meaning that very few European medical countermeasures reached the market at the peak of the pandemic. A further weakness identified was that Europe did not partici- pate in any of the pivotal efficacy trials leading to licensure. To address this situation, the European Commission established the Health Emergency Preparedness and Response Authority (HERA) as one of its Directorates General, with the mission of strengthening the European Union’s ability to respond to major health threats through coordination, expertise and the development and procurement of medical countermeasures (MCMs). In the aftermath of the COVID-19 pandemic, HERA published a call for proposals for the creation of a European Hub for vaccine development, with the mission of developing, assessing and manufacturing vaccines for priority pathogens with epidemic and pandemic potential to ensure that Europe would be more resilient through increased preparedness. This new entity was designed to be not another institution, but rather a newly created network of existing organizations already funded by their member states to develop vaccines. The mandate of the European Vaccines Hub for Pandemic Readiness (EVH) was to create a hub able to develop and deliver vaccines end-to-end, from discovery to manufacturing. To achieve this, the EVH was expected to be organ- ized in an agile manner, allowing it to make quick decisions and to include and engage with any group from industry, biotech or academia that could contribute to development of vaccines and monoclonal antibodies against pathogens with pandemic risk. Unique new structure The EVH consortium selected for funding enabled the creation of an innovative organization that has the expertise and facilities to provide the European Union with self-sustainable and independent ability to discover, develop, assess and manufacture vaccines and antibodies against infectious diseases of epidemic and pandemic potential. This organization is based on four pillars (Fig. 1). Pillar 1 leads vaccines and monoclonal antibody discovery while advancing platforms to develop vaccines based on protein and adjuvants, on mRNA or on viral vectors. Pillar 2 drives preclinical studies to support the discovery, charac- terization and development of vaccines and monoclonal antibodies. Pillar 3 coordinates clinical development, which includes the readiness to perform ad hoc phase 1 and 2 studies and controlled human challenge studies (CHIM), with the overarching goals of putting together a network of European vaccine clinical trial centers under consented protocols and preparing to conduct large-scale phase 3 studies in collaboration with the EU ‘BE READY NOW’ project. In pillar 4, the German Center for Infection Research (DZIF) and the Center for Pandemic Vaccines and Therapeutics (ZEPAI) oversee regulatory coordination and planning of manufacturing of small-scale Good Manufacturing Practice (GMP) lots for early clinical studies, as well as large-scale manufacturing of final products. Although the primary scope of the EVH is to develop and build the capacity to deliver medical countermeasures, it is designed as an open organization that reaches out and engages with small and large vaccine manufacturers, biotech, academic groups, R&D units of pharmaceuti- cal companies, and projects and networks funded by European Union, for example through the Horizon Europe program. To achieve this, the EVH is following two noteworthy paths: the creation of an innovative public–private partnership model with industry and the promotion of ‘expression of interest’ calls for experts and specific projects, enabling the EVH to liaise with experts and collaborating centers that share a similar mission, both within and outside the European Union. The arrows below each pillar in Fig. 1 denote the continuous interchange between the EVH and the European system. Projects Priority projects for the EVH are developments that tackle infec- tious diseases with epidemic and pandemic potential relevant to the European Union. Projects are proposed by the EVH and agreed upon Comment https://doi.org/10.1038/s41590-026-02653-w Check for updates Discovery of vaccines and monoclonal antibodies Novel technology platforms for vaccine and antibody development Biotecnopolo Siena, Italy Preclinical assessment of vaccine and antibody prototypes Institut Pasteur Paris, France Preclinical studies Coordination of ambulatory clinical trials, CHIM and immunological analyses Vaccinopolis University of Antwerp, Belgium Clinical studies Reliable and well-prepared European pandemic manufacturing capacities and regulatory preparedness DZIF ZEPAI, Germany Manufacturing and regulatory Platform infrastructures EVH activities Vaccines and antibodies manufacturing plan EVH European ecosystem Pillar 1 Pillar 2 Pillar 3 Pillar 4 Fig. 1 | Schematic representation of the organization and function of the European Vaccines Hub. The organization’s base is the entirety of Europe, and it is organized in four pillars that comprise the activities necessary for end-to-end vaccine delivery. The arrows below each pillar indicate that any European entity can take or bring projects. CHIM, controlled human challenge studies. nature immunology Volume 27 | December 2026 | 2363–2365 | 2364 Comment with HERA. The initial priority pathogens identified were avian influ- enza, in particular H5N1, and monkeypox (mpox). EVH activities include building the preparedness system and testing it. Indeed, the EVH’s mission creates a system that allows continuous delivery and regular updates for priorities. A living EU Epidemic and Pandemic Vaccine Readiness Plan agreed to with HERA generates an agile basis for EU pandemic preparedness. One year after the EVH was established, each of the four pillars has initiated a variety of projects and delivered important results. Pillar 1 discovered a potent and broadly protective monoclonal anti- body against mpox that recognizes a vaccine antigen not previously known to induce neutralizing antibodies. In vivo and in vitro studies in collaboration with pillar 2 confirmed that the mpox monoclonal antibody and the vaccine antigen are protective in vivo and are good candidates for continued MCM development. Pillar 3 has designed and fully enrolled a clinical trial to study the vaccine response of the European population to primary and booster immunization against the avian influenza H5N1, and is currently assessing its outcome. In the trial, H5N1-naive participants and participants immunized in 2006 with a H5N1 vaccine received an adjuvanted vaccine against the current Astrakhan clade. The study has the additional scope to establish a study cohort whose peripheral blood cells can be used to discover broadly neutralizing antibodies that recognize epitopes shared between the 2006 and 2026 H5N1 strains. Pillar 4 is addressing important bottlenecks in preparedness by mapping the European GMP facilities ready to manufacture vaccines and monoclonals for small-scale clinical trials and developing concepts for rapid ramp-up to large-scale manufacturing in pandemic crises. Its regulatory experts are addressing the anticipated practical and scientific regulatory questions required for accelerating development of EVH products to enable early availability of products. In addition, the EVH has initiated collaborations with external entities. One involves joint participation with Sanofi, a major Euro- pean vaccine manufacturer, in an EU tender to develop a mucosal mRNA vaccine against the H5N1 avian influenza. Another involves the publication of an ‘expression of interest’ to identify possible col- laborators that can contribute to further pandemic influenza vaccine development approaches. Stress testing While the EVH was working on setting up its organization, two unex- pected, highly lethal emerging infections were communicated by the World Health Organization in May 2026. The first was the Andes hanta- virus outbreak, reported on 2 May, involving a cruise ship coming out of Argentina1, and the second was the Ebola Bundibugyo outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo and Uganda that was declared a Public Health Emergency of International Concern on 17 May2. Although these were not imminent threats for Europe, after rapid consultation with HERA, it was agreed that it would be important for Europe to par- ticipate in the development of countermeasures for these viruses. The question was whether the EVH had the capacity to address these two targets that, up to that moment, had never been considered. Consultation of the EVH network identified a broadly protective human monoclonal antibody against Andes hantavirus discovered in a Swedish patient infected with Puumala hantavirus, which had been characterized by several German academic groups and whose structure had been determined a few years ago at the Institut Pasteur in Paris3. This antibody had been acquired and improved by two US R&D enterprises but was never brought into clinical development. Concurrently, the German Center for Infection Research (DZIF) labora- tories revealed recent results identifying a potent human monoclonal antibody that neutralizes both Ebola Zaire and Ebola Bundibugyo. The antibody had been shown to protect mice from challenge with the virus in the Biosafety Level 4 (BSL4) facility in Marburg4. As such, in less than a month, the two antibodies were selected by the EVH for development up to clinical testing. For antibody expression, EVH is developing an innovative platform based on the C1 fungus, which is expected to enable cost-effective production of large quantities of monoclonal antibodies, making these therapies more accessible to at-risk populations and to low-income countries at an affordable and equitable cost5. The stress test arising from the unexpected outbreaks showed that the EVH can leverage the ad hoc development of a multitude of innova- tive prototypes from excellent European entities that have hitherto failed to translate them into products when working in isolation. The EVH can turn these product candidates into countermeasures to protect people’s health. Moreover, the EVH network had at its disposal two vac- cine prototypes for the development of an Ebola vaccine: an MVA-based vaccine against Ebola Zaire developed by DZIF-associated EVH mem- bers, previously shown to be protective in a mouse challenge study performed at the Marburg BSL-4 facility6, and a measles vector-based pan-filovirus vaccine in development at the Institut Pasteur. Once added to the EVH portfolio, these projects could become highly relevant in the race against Bundibugyo virus. Furthermore, monoclonal antibodies candidates could provide an important complementary strategy, with the advantage of providing immediate protection. Looking to the future In conclusion, the EVH is an organization rooting pandemic prepar- edness within an innovative cross-sectorial ecosystem, which in its first year of existence has shown the potential to deliver innovative countermeasures. We can probably describe the EVH as both a dis- covery and development engine and a catalyst able to aggregate the best European competencies and discoveries, transforming them into medical products that include vaccines and monoclonal antibodies. The big question is whether the EVH will be able to exploit this poten- tial and deliver real products. There are numerous challenges that could interfere with this ambitious goal. One of the most important limitations is the fact that the products in the EVH portfolio do not have an immediate attractive commercial market value because they address infectious diseases that are rare, or pandemics that we hope will never happen. The absence of immediate commercial value, com- monly defined as a market failure, is a recurrent problem for most medical countermeasures. In the absence of an expected immediate and secure return on investment, the private sector is little inclined to start rapid development and manufacturing programs. Notwithstand- ing that complication, the instruments developed by the EU in terms of stockpiling essential and possibly innovative MCMs and the constant readiness of the reality-tested joint procurement mechanism are robust attempts to provide solutions to these problems. Although we have the technology to develop effective products against most infectious diseases, these need to become available for wide implementation despite the absence of immediate pre- dictable markets.
